cards.title: Match creative test volume to daily budget
cards.claim: Creative testing volume should be matched to the ad budget; small daily budgets cannot support an unlimited number of ads getting enough spend to learn.
cards.action: For small budgets, test a focused batch and give Facebook enough opportunity to distribute spend and produce a signal, rather than launching many ads.
applies_when: the goal is to learn from creative testing
do_not_use_when: you can give an unlimited number of ads enough spend to learn
unknowns: Exact number of ads for a focused batch
Exact spend threshold where more creative volume becomes viable
evidence_quotes: You have to match your creative testing volume to your budget.
if you're spending 30, 50, $100 a day, you can't feed an unlimited number of ads enough spend to actually learn anything.
I'd rather test a focused batch and give Facebook enough opportunity to distribute spend and give me some kind of signal.

cards.title: Run apples-to-apples creative tests and isolate one variable
cards.claim: A creative should not be crowned a winner just because it drives the most sales if it is the only ad that received spend; comparisons need equal visibility and isolated variables.
cards.action: Test two ad ideas in an apples-to-apples environment, allow equal visibility, and then look at data to identify why something was better; after identifying winners, test one variable at a time and keep enough things stable to isolate learning.
applies_when: testing two ad ideas such as UGC video and carousel
same angle, same product, same argument, different opening
do_not_use_when: one ad is the only thing that got spend
changing hook, angle, audience, landing page, offer, campaign, and creative all at the same time
unknowns: Exact required equal visibility or spend per variant
Minimum test duration or sample size
evidence_quotes: make sure you test them in an apples-to-apples environment like this creative test and allow them to get equal visibility and then look at the data to identify why something was better.
Don't just let one ad get the spend and assume that this is your winner.
after we identify our winning ads, we want to do one variable at a time.
If I change the hook, the angle, the audience here, the landing page, the offer, the campaign, the creative all at the same time, well, what did we test? Nothing, really.
whenever possible, I want to keep enough things stable so that I can actually isolate what I'm learning.

cards.title: Diagnose creative by customer journey, not just CTR or CPA
cards.claim: High CTR alone does not mean a creative is working; an ad can get high attention and CTR but little buying behavior if it does not explain the product and value.
cards.action: Use supporting metrics and ask whether the ad got attention, whether people clicked to the site, and what happened after the click; do not judge creative solely by CPA or ROAS, and do not blame the creative right away if an ad gets quality clicks but nobody buys.
applies_when: evaluating why a creative won or lost
an ad has high CTR but weak buying behavior
looking at CTR, link click-through rate, CPM, CPA, ROAS, and post-click data
do_not_use_when: judging creative solely by CPA or ROAS
assuming high CTR alone proves the creative works
unknowns: Thresholds for good supporting metrics beyond the example
How to attribute post-click outcomes if multiple factors changed
